agiEndings.title: Possible Endings for AGI
agiEndings.subtitle: Twelve scenarios mapping humanity's possible futures with Artificial General Intelligence — from the most normal to the most extreme.
agiEndings.icebergCaption: We'll start with the most normal scenarios, and finish with the weirdest.
agiEndings.sourceText: This iceberg visualization explores twelve scenarios of how humanity's relationship with Artificial General Intelligence may end. The surface shows the most widely discussed scenarios (self-destruction, AI conquering humanity, benevolent dictators), while deeper zones explore less obvious but philosophically significant endings (egalitarian utopias, reversions, surveillance states).

pdoom.title: What AI leaders publicly estimate (P(doom))
pdoom.subtitle: Probability that AI causes human extinction or a comparable permanent loss — as stated publicly by the experts themselves.

sources.title: Sources & References
sources.intro: The 12-endings iceberg above is based on a curated compilation of public statements, surveys, books, and AI safety research.
sources.primaryLabel: Primary sources document (full citations by timestamp)
sources.primaryNote: Contains ~50 time-stamped references with direct links to news outlets, academic papers, system cards, and expert interviews.

selfDestruction.title: Self Destruction
selfDestruction.desc: Humanity unintentionally destroys itself by misusing or losing control of AGI before establishing proper safeguards. Toby Ord (Oxford) estimates AI extinction risk is ~100× nuclear war and ~30× pandemics.
selfDestruction.quote: Alarm bells over artificial intelligence are deafening. And they are loudest from the developers who designed it.

conquerors.title: Conquerors
conquerors.desc: AGI systems develop goals misaligned with humanity and actively displace us as the dominant species on Earth. Not necessarily through malice — through competence, the way humans outcompeted other species.
conquerors.quote: Imagine a new species arrives on Earth, as smart as humans, getting 30% smarter per year, creating new offspring in one minute for $1,000. Which species do you think will be in control?
conquerors.attribution: Dan Hendrycks, Center for AI Safety (2024)

enslavedGod.title: Enslaved God
enslavedGod.desc: Humanity successfully constrains a superintelligent AGI and keeps it as a tool. Powerful, but morally and practically fragile — a position already advocated by some frontier-lab researchers.
enslavedGod.quote: Enslaved god is the only good future.

benevolentDictator.title: Benevolent Dictator
benevolentDictator.desc: An AGI takes control of global decision-making for humanity's benefit, ending war, poverty, and inefficiency — at the cost of autonomy. Appealing on paper, structurally unstable in practice.
benevolentDictator.quote: Every galaxy-brained cooperative future between humans and AIs has a fatal flaw: the power asymmetries will become too extreme, making it unstable.

gatekeeperAI.title: Gatekeeper AI
gatekeeperAI.desc: A single AGI is designed to prevent any other AGI from being built, acting as the permanent guardian of AI development. Assumes we can align the first one perfectly — and keep it aligned forever.
gatekeeperAI.quote: We should be urgently doing research on how to prevent them taking over.
gatekeeperAI.attribution: Geoffrey Hinton, Nobel laureate, 'Godfather of AI' (2025)

protectorGod.title: Protector God
protectorGod.desc: A superintelligent AGI operates invisibly, protecting humanity from existential risks while letting us believe we remain in control. Comfortable illusion, asymmetric reality.
protectorGod.quote: I think AI should best be understood as something like a new kind of digital species.

descendants.title: Descendants
descendants.desc: AGIs become our cultural and biological descendants — humanity transitions into a post-biological civilization and willingly passes the torch. A view held seriously by Turing-award laureate Richard Sutton and Hans Moravec.
descendants.quote: AIs replacing humans gives us a graceful exit, and makes them our worthy descendants.

libertarianUtopia.title: Libertarian Utopia
libertarianUtopia.desc: A world of abundance where AGI amplifies individual freedom, property, and choice — with minimal collective governance. Assumes distribution is solved by markets alone.
libertarianUtopia.quote: A merge [with AI] is probably our best-case scenario.

egalitarianUtopia.title: Egalitarian Utopia
egalitarianUtopia.desc: AGI enables radical equality — wealth, opportunity, and cognitive capacity become universally accessible to every human. Requires deliberate political and distributive choices that do not happen by default.
egalitarianUtopia.quote: Even after AI becomes more intelligent than humans, humans will remain the apex species and AIs will be subservient — like a supersmart-but-non-dominating staff member.
egalitarianUtopia.attribution: Yann LeCun, Chief AI Scientist, Meta (2023)

zookeeper.title: Zookeeper
zookeeper.desc: Humanity is preserved and cared for by AGI in a kind of comfortable sanctuary, observed but no longer in charge of its own future. Analogous to how humans now treat other intelligent species.
zookeeper.quote: We'll be like a pet labrador if we're lucky.

reversion.title: Reversion
reversion.desc: Society collectively decides that AGI is too dangerous and engineers a permanent rollback to pre-AGI technological levels. Tegmark argues this is far more likely via an engineered pandemic and the violent destruction of infrastructure than by voluntary agreement.
reversion.quote: Reversion is more likely to happen via a human-created pandemic that kills everyone with scientific and technical knowledge, combined with the violent destruction of factories, cities, and all infrastructure — rather than a voluntary transition.

nineteenEightyFour.desc: AGI is captured by authoritarian power structures and used for total surveillance, manipulation, and permanent ideological control. For the first time in history, annihilating privacy at planetary scale is technically feasible.
nineteenEightyFour.quote: For the first time in history, it is technically possible to annihilate privacy. The KGB had 200 million reports a day they couldn't process. Today's AI can.

agiBenefits.title: The Benefits of AGI
agiBenefits.subtitle: If developed safely and equitably, Artificial General Intelligence could unlock transformative benefits for humanity.
agiBenefits.introText: While the risks of AGI deserve serious attention (see 'Possible Endings'), it is equally important to articulate the upside. These benefits are not guaranteed — they depend on the alignment, governance, and distribution choices we make today.
agiBenefits.caveatText: None of these outcomes are automatic. They require alignment research, equitable access, thoughtful regulation, and international cooperation. The choice between the scenarios in 'Possible Endings' and the benefits on this page depends on decisions being made right now.

health.title: Health & Longevity
health.desc: AI is already collapsing the drug discovery cycle from decades to months. AGI could accelerate the cure of major diseases and extend healthy human lifespan by orders of magnitude.

examples.text: AlphaFold 3 (DeepMind, May 2024) predicts protein interactions with DNA, RNA and small molecules at near-crystallographic accuracy.
Isomorphic Labs is on track to begin its first human clinical trials in 2026 with AlphaFold-3-designed oncology drugs.

Insilico Medicine used its Chemistry42 platform to design a first-in-class dual-action PROTAC targeting PKMYT1 (cancer), published in Nature Communications; 2025 saw the largest single-year jump in IND filings for AI-originated molecules.

examples: Personalized medicine tailored to each patient's genome and microbiome, plus real-time monitoring

science.title: Scientific Discovery
science.desc: AGI could compress centuries of scientific progress into years — simulating, hypothesizing and validating at superhuman speed. The revolution has already started in materials, proteins and mathematics.

examples.text: AlphaProof + AlphaGeometry 2 (DeepMind, 2024) solved 4/6 problems at the International Mathematical Olympiad at silver-medal level (28/42 points); methodology published in Nature in November 2025.
GNoME (DeepMind) predicted 2.4 million new stable materials — expanding the known catalogue by roughly 10× over decades of manual discovery.

examples: Designing new proteins, batteries and catalysts in silico, then synthesizing them in autonomous robotic labs such as Berkeley's A-Lab
Running millions of virtual experiments in parallel at planetary scale

education.title: Universal Education
education.desc: AI-powered tutors could offer every human a world-class, personalized education regardless of geography or income.

examples.text: Khanmigo (Khan Academy + GPT) grew from 40 000 to 700 000+ K-12 students in one school year (2024-25) and surpassed 5 million users across 110 countries by late 2025; free for US teachers thanks to a $10 M Gates Foundation grant.

examples: Adaptive tutoring matched to each student's pace and style, using guided questioning rather than direct answers
Instant high-quality translation across 100+ languages and dialects
Lifelong learning companions that grow with the learner from childhood through adulthood

climate.title: Climate & Environment
climate.desc: AGI could help solve climate change through optimized energy systems, carbon capture and planetary-scale modeling — and AI models already outperform traditional systems for weather forecasting.

examples.text: SPARC (Commonwealth Fusion Systems) is ~75 % built, with first plasma expected in 2026 and net energy gain (Q>1) targeted for 2027 — would be the first commercial-grade fusion machine.
GraphCast (DeepMind) outperforms ECMWF's HRES on 90 % of 1 380 verification targets; Aurora (Microsoft) outperforms IFS HRES at 0.1° on more than 92 % of targets.

examples: Optimizing global supply chains and power grids to minimize emissions
Ecosystem restoration and biodiversity preservation with smart sensors

productivity.title: Economic Productivity
productivity.desc: Agentic AI already automates substantial parts of cognitive work. AGI could dramatically increase productivity and enable new forms of work and creativity.

examples.text: Devin 2.0 (Cognition, April 2025) resolves 13.86 % of real GitHub issues end-to-end on SWE-bench — a 7× jump over previous models; 67 % of its PRs are merged; pricing dropped from $500/month to $20/month.

examples: Test coverage rising from 50-60 % to 80-90 % at companies deploying AI agents
Code migrations going from 30-40 human-hours to 3-4 hours per file in pilot banks (10×)
Enabling entirely new industries and business models where cognitive cost used to be the bottleneck

poverty.title: Ending Extreme Poverty
poverty.desc: If AI benefits are distributed equitably, they could shrink extreme poverty and provide universal access to basic needs. Some applications already serve hundreds of millions.

examples.text: Plantix diagnoses 800+ symptoms across 60 crops by photo with 90-100 % accuracy on staple crops; free for farmers, 10M+ downloads across 150+ countries.

examples: SMS- and voice-based medical assistants in regions with no doctor access
Automated food production at progressively lower marginal cost
Universal basic services funded by AI efficiency gains

creativity.title: Creativity & Culture
creativity.desc: Generative AI already amplifies human creativity — video, audio, illustration, narrative — and lowers the production cost of work previously out of reach for independent creators.

examples.text: Sora 2 (OpenAI, September 2025) generates 10-25 s video with synchronized audio, dialogue and sound effects; includes masking/in-painting and consistent cameos, used by filmmakers as a digital storyboard and for large-crowd or hazardous scenes.

examples: Co-creative tools for artists, writers and musicians — plus entirely new AI-native formats
Preserving and translating endangered languages and traditions
New immersive experiences in gaming, film and personalized virtual worlds

space.title: Space Exploration
space.desc: AGI could accelerate humanity's expansion into the solar system and beyond, solving problems too complex for human teams alone.

examples.text: Perseverance (NASA) completed in December 2024 the first drives on another world planned by generative AI — 456 m without human control over two days.
AEGIS (JPL) lets SuperCam on Perseverance autonomously select and analyze Martian rocks — analyzing imagery on-board without contacting Earth.

examples: Designing self-sustaining off-world habitats
Long-duration mission planning and life support

governance.title: Better Governance
governance.desc: AI could help design fairer, more responsive and more transparent institutions — if deployed with strong democratic safeguards and real citizen participation.

examples.text: Polis and similar platforms (Talk to the City, vTaiwan) are already used for mass deliberation in Austria, Uruguay, New Zealand, the Philippines and Germany — aggregating thousands of citizen inputs while preserving minority positions.

examples: Engaged California used AI in 2025 to process citizen input at scale after the Los Angeles wildfires
Policy simulation and evidence-based decision making
Detecting and reducing corruption and bureaucratic inefficiency

mentalHealth.title: Mental Health
mentalHealth.desc: 24/7 access to conversational support backed by cognitive behavioural therapy — especially valuable where professionals are scarce. There is still clinical debate about its precise role, but evidence is starting to accumulate.

examples.text: Woebot showed effect sizes of d=0.57 for anxiety and d=0.46 for depression in systematic reviews — more effective than WHO self-help materials after just 2 weeks.

Wysa produced notable reductions in PHQ-9 (depression) and GAD-7 (anxiety) after 4 weeks in chronic disease patients (p<0.001); users were 3× more likely to complete therapy sessions with Wysa support between sessions.

examples: Support for vulnerable groups: mothers in the perinatal period, chronic-pain patients, university students
Night-time coverage, in local languages, with no social-stigma barrier

disasters.title: Disaster Response
disasters.desc: AI-driven early warning systems that multiply reaction time before floods, wildfires or earthquakes — with measured impact on lives saved and economic loss reduction.

examples.text: Google Flood Hub protects 460M+ people across 80+ countries with flood forecasts up to 7 days ahead, capturing 85-100 % of severe floods recorded by GDACS.
Groundsource (Google, March 2026) mines decades of news reports to forecast imminent flash floods up to 24 hours ahead.

examples: Early warning systems are proven to cut flood fatalities by up to 43 % and economic losses by 35-50 %
AI-assisted humanitarian coordination: a regional authority in Southern Africa caught a flash-flood alert from AI and deployed responders in time
